instructor: I believe that having to write this evaluation is humiliating for me, for the instructor, and for the department. I will mention only the main problems, and enumerate them. 1. We covered two main methods in the course, Difference-in-Differences and RDD, but the instructor consistently called the first “Diff-and-Diff” instead of “Diff-in-Diff.” I need to emphasize that this wasn’t a one-time slip or a small issue: she is a tenured prof. who wrote it like this repeatedly all semester, wrote it on the board that way, and even uploaded a file titled “Diff and Diff” to Moodle. These methods are, arguably, two of the three fundamental tools in applied microeconomics, and I would have liked to discuss how we should have explored them more rigorously and properly, but I’m stuck on the fact that the instructor didn’t even teach the methods’ correct names, what hope is there for the rest of the material (brown M&M clause)?2. Our term project involved replicating a paper, and the instructor insisted we use STATA, a paid software some of us did not knew or had been taught. When we asked how to obtain it, she told us to pirate it, borrow it from someone else. Then she remembered that there must be one in Building B. I do not understand how it is okay that an instructor would encourage students to pirate software, which clearly contradicts Bilkent’s academic integrity standards. 3. We unanimously requested a 4-2 schedule (4 hours one week, 2 hours the next), but she instead scheduled 3.5hour classes every week. After low morning attendance for a few weeks, she cancelled Wednesday sessions and reduced us to two hours per week. Under the ECTS regulations, we’re supposed to have about three hours of class weekly, so irregular scheduling and cancelling hours wholesale is improper. She also kept running the classes overtime and, for some reason, scheduled two midterms only to cancel one because she was out of town. However, I think these issues are negligible compared to rest.
